subject: Output contracts & toolchain onramp
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Kevin Hsu <kevin.hsu@aurelia.health>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Output contracts & toolchain onramp

Hi Kevin / Sara,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited to get Aurelia onto streaming + tool-calling for the triage assistant. I put a concise implementation plan together and attached the first-pass JSON schema (schema-v1.json) plus a mutual action plan (MAP_vAurelia.xlsx). High-level goals: deliver structured diagnoses (JSON), wire two tool calls (patient_lookup and guideline_fetch), and validate streaming latency under 300ms tail for clinical lookups in the POC.

Immediate asks from your side:
- Confirm the sample payload size (max tokens or chars) we should expect for patient context and transcripts.
- Any restrictions on outbound API calls from our tool-caller to your infra (IP allowlist, proxy)?
- Provide an engineer for a 30–60m sync next week to review the schema and the tool contract.

Proposal (timeline):
1) Week 0 (this week) — finalize schema + security checklist.
2) Week 1 — sandbox wiring: tool-call endpoints + streaming test harness (staging).
3) Week 2 — 3-day POC validation with synthetic traffic and one small pilot cohort.

Key implementation notes:
- Structured output: the attached schema defines top-level "encounter_id", "events[]", and a typed "recommendations" block (see schema-v1.json). We recommend returning machine-parseable arrays rather than free text for the triage step to simplify downstream ingestion.
- Tool-calling: plan for two sync HTTP calls from the model agent; we’ll provide an OpenAPI-style adapter mapping in the next revision.
- Streaming: we will stream partial JSON patches as they are produced; client should be able to accept chunked JSON / or rehydrate on the final message.

Next steps / owners:
- Aurelia: assign 1x eng (API owner) + security contact (due by 2026-10-14).
- Redwood: Monica will own project coordination, Rishi will lead runtime parameters and schema enforcement, Stephanie will own billing/entitlement and access for Dedicated if needed.

Proposed sync times (PDT): Tue 2026-10-13 11:00 or Wed 2026-10-14 09:00 — let me know which works and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Attachments: schema-v1.json (application/json), MAP_vAurelia.xlsx (spreadsheet).

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
m: 415-555-0117
https://redwood.ai

From: Kevin Hsu <kevin.hsu@aurelia.health>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@aurelia.health>
Date: 2026-10-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Output contracts & toolchain onramp

Monica — thanks for the clear plan and the attachments. Two quick clarifications before we lock in the sync: 

1) Payload: our front-end sends ~2.5KB average (notes + vitals) and peaks at ~25KB for multi-encounter transcripts. Will that fit your streaming assumptions?
2) Tool-calls: patient_lookup needs to include our internal token-based auth; we prefer a reverse-proxy (company-managed) over exposing internal IPs. Can your tool agent call out via a customer-managed proxy?
3) Security: I attached our partially filled security questionnaire (Aurelia_SecQ_filled.pdf). We’ll need SOC2 artifacts and evidence of request-level audit logs retained for 90 days.

We can do Tue 11:00 (Oct 13) — Sara (Engineering Manager) will join.

On Mon, Oct 12, 2026 at 9:12 AM Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai> wrote:
> [Quoted earlier message omitted]

Thanks,
Kevin Hsu
Head of Partnerships | Aurelia Health
kevin.hsu@aurelia.health

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Kevin Hsu <kevin.hsu@aurelia.health>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-13T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Output contracts & toolchain onramp — answers + attachments

Kevin / Sara — great questions. Quick answers and next steps below. I’ve attached schema-v1.json (inline reference) and updated the MAP with named owners.

Payload sizing:
- 25KB peak is acceptable for the POC. We’ll configure the runtime to chunk by 16KB windows and stream JSON patches. That configuration keeps per-token overhead low while preserving final structure.

Tool-calls and proxying:
- Yes — Redwood’s tool agent can egress via a customer-managed reverse proxy. We typically ask for a short-lived mTLS client cert or an IP allowlist + proxy endpoint. Rishi, can you confirm the exact headers/auth we recommend?

Security artifacts & logging:
- We can provide SOC2 Type II report summary, and request-level audit logs (request_id, timestamp, model, route) retained for 90 days. We’ll share a sample logs extract in the sandbox after initial wiring.

Sample schema excerpt (from attached schema-v1.json):
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "encounter_id": {"type": "string"},
    "events": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object"}},
    "recommendations": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {"type": "object", "properties": {"code": {"type": "string"}, "confidence": {"type": "number"}}}
    }
  },
  "required": ["encounter_id", "events"]
}

Pilot plan (concrete):
- Tue 2026-10-13: schema walk (30m) + proxy cert exchange (30m).
- Wed 2026-10-14 to Fri 2026-10-16: sandbox validation with 10 test encounters / minute. Run two tool-call scenarios and one streaming-only flow.
- End of week: quick regression check and plan for limited pilot rollout.

Links: Redwood streaming docs — https://redwood.ai/docs/streaming-onboarding#tool-calls (see section: proxy egress). I’ll also upload SOC2 summary to the shared Drive prior to the sync.

I’ll send a calendar invite for Tue 11:00 PDT. One ask for the sync: please include an engineer who can talk through the proxy termination and sample API responses.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments: schema-v1.json (application/json), MAP_vAurelia.xlsx (updated)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Kevin Hsu <kevin.hsu@aurelia.health>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-14T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Output contracts & toolchain onramp — runtime notes

Quick technical note from runtime:
- For the POC, enable prefix/KV caching for the patient_lookup path (TTL 10m) to keep latency sub-300ms for repeated lookups.
- Model variant suggestion: use redwood-rl-7b-q5 for POC to reduce cost; if you need longer context and structured fidelity, we can switch to redwood-llama-70b-q4 for the pilot cohort.
- For streaming, we’ll emit partial JSON "patch" events with an incrementing sequence number. Client should ACK the final seq. We’ll include "request_id" in every chunk for auditability.

I’ll prepare a short runtime config snippet and drop it into the shared Drive before the sync.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Lead, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
